questions.question: A bus starts from a bus stand after every 50 minutes in the same direction. Mohit is walking in opposite direction with a speed of 50 km/hr. If Mohit meets each bus in 10 minutes, then what is the speed of bus?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The distance covered by the bus in (50 − 10) = 40 minutes is equal to the distance covered by Mohit in 10 minutes.

Since the distance is constant, Speed is inversely proportional to Time.

Ratio of Time (Bus : Mohit) = 40 : 10 = 4 : 1

Ratio of Speed (Bus : Mohit) = 1 : 4

Mohit's speed = 4 units ⇒ 50 km/hr, so Bus's speed = 1 unit ⇒ 50 ÷ 4 = 12.5 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 12.5 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Bus frequency time = 50 mins

Mohit's meeting time with each bus = 10 mins

Mohit's speed = 50 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction) = S₁ + S₂

 
• Next Bus Mohit Meet in 10 mins 
 
 Bus travels for 10 mins Mohit travels for 10 mins 
• 
• 
• Initial Gap = Bus Speed × 50 mins 
 
 

**Calculations:**

Let the speed of the bus be V km/hr.

⇒ Distance between two consecutive buses = V × (50/60) km

⇒ Relative speed of Bus and Mohit = (V + 50) km/hr

⇒ Time taken to meet = 10/60 hours

We know, Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

⇒ 10/60 = [V × (50/60)] ÷ (V + 50)

⇒ 1/6 = (5V/6) ÷ (V + 50)

⇒ (V + 50) / 6 = 5V / 6

⇒ V + 50 = 5V

⇒ 4V = 50

⇒ V = 12.5

**∴ The correct answer is 12.5 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two bodies are moving in opposite directions towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two bodies are moving in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (|S₁ − S₂|).

Distance in Periodic Events

If a bus or train departs periodically after every T interval, the constant distance maintained between any two consecutive vehicles on the route is D = Speed × T.

questions.question: The speed of a train including stoppages is 75 kmph and excluding stoppages, the speed of the train is 90 kmph. For how many minutes does the train stop per hour?

Stoppage time per hour = [(Faster Speed − Slower Speed) ÷ Faster Speed] × 60 min

Stoppage time per hour = (15 ÷ 90) × 60

Stoppage time per hour = (1 ÷ 6) × 60 = 10 minutes

questions.question: A boy starts from his house and walks at a speed of 5 km/hr and reaches his school 3 minutes late. Next day he starts at the same time and increases his speed by 4 km/hr and reaches 3 minutes early. What is the distance (in km) between the school and his house?
questions.solution:
Let the distance between the school and his house be ‘x’ km

Time taken on first day = Distance/speed = x/5 hrs.

His speed on next day = 5 + 4 = 9 km/hr.

Time taken on next day = x/9 hrs.

Now,

∵ He reached 3 min. late on the first day and reached 3 min. early the next day, this means that the difference between the time taken on the 2 days = 3 + 3 = 6 min. = 6/60 = 1/10 hrs.

⇒ x/5 – x/9 = 1/10

⇒ (9x – 5x)/45 = 1/10

⇒ 4x/45 = 1/10

⇒ x = 45/4 × 1/10

⇒ x = 1.125 km

∴ Distance between the school and his house is 1.125 km

questions.question: A man travels a certain distance at 12 km/h and returns to the starting point at 9 km/h. The total time taken by him for the entire journey is 2(1)/(3) hours. The total distance (in km) covered by him is:
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Let the distance traveled be 2x.

Distance traveled in each directions = x 

Since, Time taken = Distance/Speed

According to the question,

⇒ x/12 + x/9 = 7/3

⇒ x = 12 km

**∴ The total distance travelled by the man = 2 × 12 = 24 km (Forward and**

**backward)**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Formula used:**

Average speed = 2ab/(a + b)

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculation:**

Average speed = 2 × 12 × 9/(12 + 9)

⇒ 2 × 12 × 9/21

⇒ 72/7 km/h

Distance = (72/7) × (7/3)

⇒ 24 km

**∴ The required distance is 24 km.**

questions.question: A train covers a certain distance in 45 minutes. If its speed is reduced by 5 km/h, it takes 3 minutes more to cover the same distance. The distance (in km) is:
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Let the distance be D km

Speed = Distance/Time = D/(45/60) = 60D/45 = (4D/3) km/h

The speed of train is reduced by 5 km/h

∴ New speed = (4D/3) – 5 = (4D – 15)/3 km/h

New time = 45min + 3min = 48min

48/60 × (4D – 15)/3 = D

⇒ 16 (4D – 15) = 60D

⇒ 4 (4D – 15) = 15D

⇒ 16D – 60 = 15D

⇒ D = 60

∴ The distance = 60 km 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

If speed reduced by 5 km/hr, so total time taken is (45 + 3) = 48 min

questions.question: During his morning walk, Atul walks for 45 minutes at a speed of 8 km/h and takes 15 rounds of a park. Shekhar takes 10 rounds of the same park in 40 minutes. What is the speed of Shekhar in km/h?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of Atul = 8 km/h

Shekhar completes 10 rounds in 40 minutes

**Concept used:**

Distance = Speed × time

Using unitary method to solve question

**Calculation:**

In 45 minutes Atul cover 8 × 45/60 = 6 km

So, 15 rounds = 6 km

So, 10 rounds = 4 km

So, Shekhar covers 4 km in 40 minutes

So, his speed is 6 km/h

**∴**** The speed of Shekhar is 6 km/h**
